CONFIDENTIAL SEPARATION AGREEMENT - T. Brzozowski - Draft 4 (matter NGS 0417-0093)

CONFIDENTIAL SEPARATION AGREEMENT AND GENERAL RELEASE
This Confidential Separation Agreement and General Release (the "Agreement") is made between Hartsfield Cold Chain Logistics, Inc., a Georgia corporation with its principal office at 2750 Fulton Industrial Boulevard SW, Atlanta, Georgia 30336 ("Hartsfield" or the "Company"), and Thaddeus J. Brzozowski of 418 Wieuca Trace NE, Atlanta, GA 30342 ("Employee" or "Mr. Brzozowski"), Employee No. HCC-004418. The Company and Employee are together the "Parties."
1. Separation
1.1 Employee's employment as Vice President, Network Operations began on August 14, 2006 and will end on February 27, 2026 (the "Separation Date"). Employee has been on approved medical leave since 11/03/2025 following coronary artery bypass surgery and the Parties agree that he will not return to active duty before the Separation Date.
1.2 The Company will describe the separation, internally and externally, as a position elimination resulting from the consolidation of its Savannah and Macon hubs. Desmond Quach, Chief Operating Officer, will send the announcement in the form attached as Exhibit C and no other announcement will be made without Employee's written approval, which he will not unreasonably withhold.
1.3 Effective on the Separation Date Employee resigns as an officer of the Company and as a manager of Hartsfield Reefer Leasing LLC (EIN 58-2204417), and agrees to sign any further document reasonably needed to record those resignations.
2. Accrued Amounts
Whether or not Employee signs this Agreement, on the first regular payday after the Separation Date, March 6, 2026, the Company will pay: (a) base salary earned through the Separation Date at the annual rate of $214,000; (b) 137.5 hours of accrued, unused PTO, being $14,146.63; and (c) expense report ER-25-1187 in the amount of $1,904.18, less the personal charges identified in Section 6.1.
3. Severance
3.1 In exchange for the release in Section 7, and provided Employee does not revoke under Section 8, the Company will pay severance equal to 39 weeks of base salary, $160,500.00 gross (the "Severance Pay"), in 19 bi-weekly installments, less applicable withholdings, on the following schedule:
Installment	Pay date	Gross
1	03/20/2026	$8,447.37
2	04/03/2026	$8,447.37
3-18	every second Friday	$8,447.37 each
19 (final)	11/27/2026	$8,447.34

3.2 The Company will pay Employee's 2025 annual bonus at 18% of base salary, $38,520, in a lump sum on or before March 13, 2026.
3.3 The Company will pay an additional lump sum of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000.00) in resolution of the matters described in Section 7.2. This amount will be reported on Form 1099-MISC. All other payments will be reported on Form W-2 under the Social Security number on file ending -5708.
3.4 Payments will be made by direct deposit to Employee's account at Ashgrove Federal Credit Union, routing no. 113493384, account ending 40977. Any change must be requested in writing to Latisha Kimathi, Director of People Operations, at lkimathi@hartsfieldcc.example.
4. Benefits
4.1 Group health coverage through Verity Mutual Health (group VMH-G-20771, subscriber ID W7 3391 0048) ends on February 28, 2026. If Employee timely elects COBRA continuation for himself and his spouse, Carolyn Brzozowski, the Company will pay the employer share of the premium, $1,318.44 per month, through November 30, 2026 or, if earlier, the date Employee becomes eligible under another group plan. The Parties acknowledge that Mrs. Brzozowski is in active treatment for multiple sclerosis and that uninterrupted coverage is a material term.
4.2 Contributions to the 401(k) plan stop on the Separation Date. Employee's account with Orchard Retirement Services, participant no. 0044-718-2260, is fully vested. The outstanding plan loan balance of $11,260.09 is repayable under the plan's terms and is not forgiven by this Agreement.
4.3 The Company will pay for up to six months of outplacement services with Linden Career Transitions, not to exceed $7,500, on invoices sent directly to the Company.
4.4 Nothing in this Agreement affects Employee's pending short-term disability claim STD-2025-118834 or the vested pension he earned in his earlier service as a union dock steward.
5. Equity
Grant	Grant date	Options	Strike	Vested at Separation Date
NQ-0611	06/01/2019	12,000	$4.10	12,000
NQ-0902	03/15/2022	8,000	$7.85	6,000
RSU-0147	01/10/2024	3,500	N/A	1,750 (accelerated)

The post-termination exercise period for vested options is extended to August 26, 2026. Unvested awards are forfeited on the Separation Date.
6. Company Property
6.1 On or before March 4, 2026 Employee will return the following to Yusuf Kaplan, IT Asset Coordinator (404-555-0188):
Item	Identifier	Notes
Laptop, Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon	S/N PW-08KR3T; tag HCC-A-20931	with dock and charger
iPhone 14 Pro	IMEI 357828169645374	the number (404) 555-0126 may be ported to Employee
Building badge	0027714	Atlanta HQ and Savannah hub
Fuel card	ending 3068, embossed THADDEUS BRZOZOWSKI	cancel on receipt
Corporate Amex	XXXX-XXXXXX-83734	personal charges of $2,318.70 to be deducted under Section 2(c)
Company vehicle	2024 Ford Explorer, VIN 1FMSK8DH4RGA51207, tag TXR 4471	see Section 6.2

6.2 Employee may purchase the vehicle for $31,200 by notice given on or before March 31, 2026. Otherwise he will return it to the Macon motor pool with both keys and the toll transponder, no. 0094 5521 873.
6.3 Employee's network account tbrzozowski, his VPN profile and his WMS login TJB_OPS01 will be disabled at 6:00 p.m. on the Separation Date. Employee confirms that he has not kept Company data on any personal device or in his personal mail account tadbrz61@mailbox.example, and he will give the iPhone passcode (440816) to Mr. Kaplan when the phone is returned.
7. Release
7.1 Employee, for himself and his heirs, releases the Company, its affiliates and their officers, directors, employees and agents (the "Releasees") from all claims of any kind arising on or before the date he signs this Agreement, including claims under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act, the Americans with Disabilities Act, the Family and Medical Leave Act, ERISA, the Age Discrimination in Employment Act (29 U.S.C. § 621 et seq.) and the common law of any state.
7.2 The release specifically includes the matters raised in the December 9, 2025 letter from Employee's counsel, which alleged that he was selected for elimination because of his heart condition and his age, and EEOC Charge No. 410-2026-00733, which Employee will ask the agency to withdraw within 5 business days after the Effective Date. The Company denies those allegations.
7.3 Not released: Employee's workers' compensation claim WC-GA-2021-448120 (the 2021 forklift injury to his left knee), vested benefits, rights to indemnification as a former officer, and any claim that cannot lawfully be waived.
7.4 Employee represents that he is not a Medicare beneficiary and is not a debtor in any pending bankruptcy case. He has disclosed that a Chapter 13 plan confirmed in 2017 was completed and discharged.
8. Review and Revocation
8.1 Employee acknowledges, as required by the Older Workers Benefit Protection Act, that he is over 40; that he was first given this Agreement on February 6, 2026; that he has at least 21 days to consider it; that he has been advised in writing to consult a lawyer and has consulted Sandor Szabo of Szabo Holloway LLC; and that he signs voluntarily.
8.2 Employee may revoke within 7 days after signing by written notice to Priscilla Nasser, Nasser Giroux & Stern LLP, at pnasser@ngslaw.example. The eighth day after signing, if there is no revocation, is the "Effective Date."
8.3 Within ten days after the Effective Date the Company will pay $9,750.00 toward Employee's legal fees by wire to the IOLTA account of Szabo Holloway LLC at Peachleaf Bank & Trust, ABA 116816670, account 2200 4471 9035, reference "Brzozowski / SH-26-0112".
9. Restrictive Covenants
9.1 For 12 months after the Separation Date Employee will not provide refrigerated-warehousing or reefer-fleet management services, in a role similar to the one he held with the Company, within Fulton, Chatham, Bibb or Clayton Counties for Frostline Distribution Partners or Glacier Gate Logistics. The Parties intend this covenant to comply with O.C.G.A. § 13-8-50 et seq.
9.2 For the same period Employee will not solicit any Company employee who reported to him, directly or through one other person, during his last two years of employment.
9.3 Confidential Information includes the pricing, volumes and service levels for the Sweetbay Grocers account, which the Parties agree is worth approximately $18.4 million a year to the Company, and Employee will not use or disclose it.
9.4 Mutual Non-Disparagement. Employee will not disparage the Company. The Company will instruct Imogen Rautio, Mr. Quach and Ms. Kimathi not to disparage Employee. Reference inquiries will be directed to Ms. Kimathi at 404.555.0102, who will confirm dates of employment and last title only.
10. Tax
The Parties intend all payments to be exempt from or to comply with Section 409A. The Company makes no representation about the tax treatment of any payment and Employee is responsible for his own taxes other than amounts the Company withholds.
11. Miscellaneous
11.1 Governing Law. This Agreement is governed by Georgia law. Any action will be brought in the state or federal courts sitting in Fulton County.
11.2 Entire Agreement. This Agreement, with Exhibit A and Exhibit C, is the entire agreement of the Parties on its subject and replaces the offer letter dated July 21, 2006. Exhibit B is an internal note and is not part of the Agreement.
11.3 Notices will be sent by email and overnight courier as follows:
To	Address	Email
Company	Attn: General Counsel, 2750 Fulton Industrial Boulevard SW, Atlanta, GA 30336	legal@hartsfieldcc.example
Employee	418 Wieuca Trace NE, Atlanta, GA 30342; after June 1, 2026: 77 Marsh Wren Court, St. Simons Island, GA 31522	tadbrz61@mailbox.example
Employee's counsel	Sandor Szabo, 1180 Peachtree Street NE, Suite 2450, Atlanta, GA 30309; tel. 404-555-0159	sszabo@szaboholloway.example

Signatures
